newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan unions unhappy with new minimum salary.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan unions unhappy with new minimum salary.

text.p: Venezuela's largest union said Wednesday a 44 percent increase in the minimum salary to 75,000 bolivars ($156) per month was still too low.

"It is insufficient because 75,000 bolivars virtually does not cover half the cost of basic food requirements," Carlos Navarro, secretary general of the Venezuelan Workers Confederation (CTV), told Union Radio.
The CTV had been calling for the minimum wage to be raised from 53,000 bolivars ($110) to 90,000 bolivars ($188) per month.
Navarro said that while unions would not turn down the proposed increase, they would continue to fight for a higher minimum wage.
